All changes in this chapter implement safety limits on the nesting depth of ESQL expressions and query plans to prevent potential stack overflow vulnerabilities (DoS). The implementation follows a robust pattern using `try...finally` blocks to ensure that depth counters are correctly decremented regardless of whether parsing succeeds or fails.
The accompanying tests in `#PG42R` comprehensively cover various ways to trigger these limits (casts, mathematical operators, boolean logic, and parentheses), ensuring the boundaries are correctly enforced. Additionally, the updates to `HeapAttackIT` (`#5EG5D`, `#XRJHQ`, `#03MFV`) correctly adjust existing integration tests so they do not inadvertently trigger these new parser limits when testing other mechanisms like circuit breakers.

review_comment: We need a good explanation in docs about this limitation, because `abs(12)` can be considered as one expression by the end user. `abs(abs(12))` - 2 expressions and so on. In total we have a query that is made of MAX_EXPRESSION_DEPTH / 2 expressions. OR we define MAX_EXPRESSION_DEPTH as 250 and everything we check (expressionbuidler and tests will be against MAX_EXPRESSION_DEPTH * 2).

In this specific case it's `abs(a + 12)` (and recursively `abs(abs(a + 12) + 12)`) that is actually two expressions, so the test is coherent with  MAX_EXPRESSION_DEPTH.
We definitely need an explanation for the parentheses alone (eg. `(a)` see my [other comment](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/108089/files#r1584808445) above), because in that case it's really only one expression that accounts for two. I guess we can clarify it in the docs.
